inputs.text: They’re presenting this as a spontaneous stand against the far right, but an event organised by hundreds of groups, including unions and Muslim representative bodies, just weeks before local elections looks more like a coordinated effort to steer the political conversation. The timing—six months after one of Britain’s largest-ever far-right demonstrations—helps keep that threat front and centre. I wouldn’t take the official framing at face value: mass rallies can be used to define which views are acceptable and shape voters before they reach the polls.
